prior_attempt: The link fragment was processed and a POST reached /redeem. Automated browser diagnostics showed method POST from a top-level HTTPS document, but native form navigation sent an opaque null Origin. The exact-Origin guard correctly returned 403 before rate limiting or Durable Object access. The same response was reproduced against the deployed Worker without retaining request values, cookies, link material or IP.
diagnosis: Safari received Rejected because the native form handoff produced Origin: null, which did not equal the request URL origin. The fragment regex and token/session pairing were valid; the Worker was reached. The strict guard was correct to reject an opaque origin.
fix: The handoff now removes the fragment, then uses credentialed same-origin Fetch API POST. HTTPS, host, exact Origin, POST, content type, bounded body, rate limit, session/token hash, expiry and atomic Durable Object consumption are unchanged.
verification: Automated browser test against deployed version 70ead5f1-ba82-4205-9084-6652d99c4a86 passed: one-use handoff POST returned 303, clean URL and secure HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie appeared, and replay returned 404. Public contact remains disabled.
secret_handling: Link URL stays only in the owner's mode-0600 file and interactive Termius output. Fragment is not included in HTTP requests. The Worker secret stores only a hash and session/expiry metadata. No auth material is written to logs, Git, or analytics.
next: A final 30-minute link has been prepared only after the deployed end-to-end proof; owner may now continue the human Turnstile scenarios. No prior human tests were repeated.
